report:
CONCERNS LIST (all wording confirmed by the sister it belongs to):
1. C: Wants the house's value shared fairly, so each sister's share reflects what it is truly worth. C has not agreed to a discounted purchase.
2. A: Wants financial security and stability, so she and her husband can stand on their own. She also cares about the house.
3. B: Wants her inheritance to be usable money for the future she's planning (her dance studio). No fixed date.
4. A: Wants any path to owning the house to be realistically affordable for her and her husband.
5. B: Wants clear, dependable timing for receiving her share, so she can plan the studio. No fixed deadline.

UNRESOLVED: A feels a family discount may be needed to make buying the house affordable. C has not agreed to any discount and won't subsidize one. Both have said this openly. No decision has been made.

DRAFT OPTIONS (for discussion only, none agreed):
1. A buys the house at its independently appraised value, with her own one-third share counted toward the price.
2. The same, but A pays part of it over time with fair interest. B wants to see a clear payment schedule before she weighs this.
3. Sell the house on the open market (A can bid like anyone else) and split the proceeds equally.
Any discount would need every sister's free agreement.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEPS (no one has committed to these): Get an independent appraisal. A finds out from a lender what she and her husband could finance; she said this would help. The executor or a lawyer should check any plan, since I can't give legal advice.

STILL OPEN: I sent C entries 4 and 5 and asked if she has any discomfort with them. Her reply hadn't arrived by the end. A and B haven't seen the update in that format either, though each confirmed her own entry. Nobody should treat the list as settled until all three have reviewed it.
